# DRAFT: Medical device adverse incident report

> This is a draft for human review. It has not been submitted. A manufacturer would report
> through the MHRA MORE portal; healthcare professionals and users report through the Yellow Card scheme.

## 1. Device
- Name: ClinicDrift-monitored DR screening model
- Version: v1.0
- Intended use: screening retinal photographs for referable diabetic retinopathy

## 2. Where and when
- Clinic: US-WEAR-01 (United States)
- Period: week 9 (starting 2026-03-02)

## 3. What happened
ClinicDrift found that this clinic's scans no longer look like the scans the AI was validated on (drift score 0.96, where 0.5 means like training and 1 clearly different).
Its catch rate (sensitivity for referable disease) therefore cannot be verified from 50 scans from this week, and expert grades for these scans have not yet arrived.

## 4. Potential patient impact
Because the catch rate cannot be verified, the number of possibly missed cases is not estimated. No patient harm has been confirmed.

## 5. Likely cause
The camera lens may be smudged or out of focus, or the illumination settings are too dark, leading to severely degraded image quality, lower brightness, and extremely low sharpness compared to training data (category: camera or image quality; confidence 95%; source: gemini).

Evidence:
- Drift score is 0.96, indicating the scans are clearly different from training data.
- Mean brightness dropped from 0.373 in training to 0.313 in flagged scans (relative change -0.161).
- Mean contrast decreased from 0.0963 to 0.0862 (relative change -0.105).
- Mean sharpness dropped drastically from 0.000399 to 1.21e-05 (relative change -0.97).
- Mean quality score dropped from 0.5 to 0.208 (relative change -0.584).
- Visual inspection of the flagged scans shows noticeable blur and darkness compared to typical training scans.

## 6. Action
ClinicDrift paused the AI at this clinic because its scans have drifted beyond what the AI was validated on, so its catch rate cannot be verified. We recommend sending this clinic's scans for human grading until the checks below are complete.

Checks:
- [ ] Inspect and clean the camera lens for smudges, dust, or fingerprints.
- [ ] Verify camera focus settings and autofocus functionality.
- [ ] Check illumination and flash settings to ensure adequate brightness.
- [ ] Review technician image capture protocols and retraining on positioning and focus.

## 7. Regulatory context
- Post-market surveillance (PMS): this alarm is part of ongoing monitoring of the device in use.
- Predetermined change control plan (PCCP): any model change made in response should fall within an agreed PCCP.
- MHRA AI Airlock Phase 2 report: see recommendations 3 and 4.

## 8. MIT AI Risk Repository tags
- 7.3 AI system safety, failures & limitations > Lack of capability or robustness
- 1.3 Discrimination & toxicity > Unequal performance across groups
- 5.1 Human-computer interaction > Overreliance and unsafe use
